variant: Character LoRA for Kyle trained on real photographs, following the Ivy route. The output is a reusable identity asset: kyle_rescue, bot_builders_champion and nightelf_hunter all carried his face by reference tokens and a master portrait, which this replaces with a trigger token.
title: Kyle — character LoRA
status: training 2026-09-26 22:02 — 20 image/caption pairs, 2000 steps, checkpoints every 400
source: 16 HEIC turnaround frames shot for this project, plus 4 photographs from nightelf_hunter and bot_builders_champion; all in raw/, which is git-ignored
notes: Kyle is Kevin's son; consent settled. Shot as a deliberate turnaround to fix the defect the Ivy LoRA ended with: her set was entirely frontal and three-quarter, so the LoRA damaged profiles and back views above weight 0.5. Kyle's set has both profiles, the back of the head and two back three-quarters. The cost is the opposite bias — one shirt, one wall, one light, one distance — mitigated with four photographs from other settings and by naming the shirt, wall and light in every caption even though they never vary, so a later prompt has a handle to override them.

dataset.subject: boy
dataset.status: built 2026-09-26, captions hand-written after viewing each frame
dataset.caption_rule: Isolation Rule — caption only what varies (framing, angle, expression, clothing, background, light). Face, hair and permanent features omitted so they bind to the trigger.
inventory: kyle_ship.jpg — medium, outdoor, overcast, patterned shirt
05_build_table.jpg — group, Kyle standing centre in a white tee; confirmed by the existing bot_builders crop
08_kyle_lindsey_parkas.jpg — full body, indoor, red parka (the only full body)
04_lunch.jpg — group, which boy is Kyle needs confirming
dataset.gaps: close framing dominates; expect the framing pull toward close-ups seen on Ivy
dataset.composition: 16 turnaround frames + 4 context photographs (warship deck, hotel breakfast, red parka full length, garage with a LEGO model)
dataset.angles: 9 frontal, 2 true profile, 2 three-quarter, 3 back or back three-quarter, 4 varied
dataset.gotcha: the HEICs carry no orientation tag and sips -r only writes a rotation hint, so the first run trained 67 steps on a sideways dataset; ROTATE= now bakes the rotation through PIL

training.measured_on_ivy: 0.22 it/s, ~2 h 35 m for 2000 steps, 402 MB per checkpoint
training.weights_from_ivy: 1.0 frontal close-up, 0.85 three-quarter and full body, 0.5-0.7 turning, <=0.5 profile or back
training.prediction: Kyle's profile and back ceiling should be much higher than Ivy's 0.5, because his dataset contains those angles. If it is not, the dataset explanation for Ivy's ceiling is wrong.
